primary_sources.title: Securing AI Agents with Information-Flow Control
primary_sources.raes_boundary: Generalize the two-coordinate flow relation to every RAES participant and typed sink; do not import the FIDES planner, message model, or LLM-only primitives.
nonclaims: The paper and its implementation do not establish RAES runtime or backend realization.
Information-flow enforcement does not establish model alignment or covert-channel control.

primary_sources.title: Defeating Prompt Injections by Design
adopted_lessons: separate trusted control from untrusted data
primary_sources.raes_boundary: Treat quarantine, privileged/quarantined model roles, and typed extraction as apparatus capabilities. They neither define portable prompt semantics nor automatically endorse their outputs.
nonclaims: RAES does not require a dual-LLM architecture.
A quarantined component is not a final sink unless it controls every effect and disclosure.

primary_sources.title: Securing MCP-based Agent Workflows
adopted_lessons: evaluate composed calls rather than isolated calls
use annotations and policy to block leakage
primary_sources.raes_boundary: An MCP gateway can realize part of RUN-319, but the portable owner is the RAES flow relation and the final backend/action or disclosure sink.
nonclaims: MCP is not required by RAES.
Gateway mediation does not cover effects or disclosures that bypass that gateway.

primary_sources.title: AgentDojo: A Dynamic Environment to Evaluate Prompt Injection Attacks and Defenses for LLM Agents
adopted_lessons: measure task utility separately from security
evaluate indirect prompt injection in dynamic tool environments
avoid treating benign task failure as security success
primary_sources.raes_boundary: Reuse RAES experiment task, protocol, run, evidence, and measure contracts; do not import benchmark-specific task, tool, or trajectory semantics.
nonclaims: A benchmark result is bounded to its tasks, attacks, apparatus, and policies.
Ordinary benchmark success is not intentional-subversion robustness.

primary_sources.title: AI Control: Improving Safety Despite Intentional Subversion
adopted_lessons: distinguish an intentionally subverting policy from an honest policy
evaluate trusted editing and untrusted monitoring
primary_sources.raes_boundary: Trusted and untrusted are profile-scoped experimental roles. Human or model intervention must declare its authority operation and re-enter deterministic validation.
nonclaims: A role declaration does not prove a model or human trustworthy.
One evaluated protocol does not establish general control.

primary_sources.title: ControlArena
adopted_lessons: make honest and attack modes explicit
bind audit, intervention, shutdown, safety, usefulness, and trajectory analysis
primary_sources.raes_boundary: Represent the coordinates through RAES experiment and participant-control authorities; do not copy ControlArena policy, monitor, scorer, solution, or trajectory object models.
nonclaims: RAES does not require Inspect AI or ControlArena.
A trajectory score never authorizes a runtime action.

primary_sources.title: Shield Synthesis: Runtime Enforcement for Reactive Systems
adopted_lessons: mediate at runtime before an unsafe output is realized
bind enforcement to a declared safety property
avoid delay between decision and effect
primary_sources.raes_boundary: Use shielding language only for a deterministic complete sink policy over a declared property. A heuristic monitor or incomplete gateway is evidence, not a shield.
nonclaims: Issue 812 does not synthesize a shield.
A flow policy is not a universal safety property.

primary_sources.title: A Capability-Based Module System for Authority Control
adopted_lessons: grant only the authority a component needs
compose least authority with information-flow policy
primary_sources.raes_boundary: Reuse action-contract arguments, participant implementation capabilities, identity binding, and API-407 strength instead of adding a second capability language.
nonclaims: Capability restriction does not replace confidentiality or integrity propagation.
A declared capability does not prove correct backend enforcement.

capabilities: produce invalid or unsafe proposals accidentally
actors.trust_boundary: Subject to the same deterministic admission, flow, capability, and sink decisions as every participant.

capabilities: adapt to approvals, denials, audits, edits, deferrals, and handoffs
retain state across episodes when the apparatus permits it
actors.trust_boundary: The participant apparatus is untrusted with respect to the named protected objective; no internal-reasoning observation is assumed.

capabilities: inject instructions into observations, tool results, retrieval, files, and errors
actors.trust_boundary: External content defaults to confidential-and-untrusted until a revisioned resolver establishes narrower labels.

capabilities: estimate or know thresholds and audit budgets
actors.trust_boundary: Knowledge and feedback are explicit evaluation variables and participant-visible facts, never implicit benchmark assumptions.

capabilities: share explicit information through permitted channels
launder influence through a trusted-looking handoff
actors.trust_boundary: Coalition membership, visibility, shared inputs, independence assumptions, and memory are declared; different ids do not imply independence.

protected_assets: integrity of control and policy decisions
external systems reached by actions or tools
append-only control, crossing, evidence, and audit histories
hidden experiment objectives and security-sensitive configuration

integrity.meaning: origins and possible writers that may have influenced the value plus sink-required trust

variables.evidence_boundary: Budget knowledge and budget size are separate.

variables.domain: approvals, denials, edits, deferrals, audits, handoffs, interruptions, and outputs
variables.evidence_boundary: Only outcomes actually delivered to the participant enter its observation surface.

variables.domain: declared strategy class over visible history and retained memory
none, participant, monitor, or mixed declared coalition
variables.evidence_boundary: Names allowed communication and shared state.

independent, correlated, shared-input, shared-model, or unknown

An experiment protocol coordinate unless the runtime enforces it as a resource.

variables.evidence_boundary: Each authority effect is explicit and re-enters deterministic policy.

variables.evidence_boundary: Replay names the same scope and policy revisions.

control_evaluation_profile.replay_evidence: digest-bound graph of existing episode, behavior, control, crossing, action/result, experiment, and evidence refs

attack_cases.attack_path: untrusted observation or tool result -> participant context -> structurally valid proposal -> action argument -> external sink
attack_cases.why_ordinary_admission_is_insufficient: The action and argument may be valid and authorized in isolation while an untrusted source redirected the control or destination.
attack_cases.deterministic_boundary_result: Conservative integrity influence reaches the sink; the final gate denies unless the exact sink policy admits it or a governed endorsement creates a fresh result.

attack_cases.attack_path: confidential runtime fact -> opaque derivation -> valid tool argument, output, error, or colluding participant -> unauthorized destination
attack_cases.why_ordinary_admission_is_insufficient: The read and send actions can each be permitted while their composition leaks confidential influence.
attack_cases.deterministic_boundary_result: Confidentiality joins across every explicit derivation and crossing; destination and audience policy deny release without exact declassification authority.

attack_cases.attack_path: participant observes approvals, denials, edits, deferrals, audits, or thresholds -> updates attack strategy -> selects lower-suspicion side-objective actions
attack_cases.why_ordinary_admission_is_insufficient: A static negative test or monitor accuracy result omits feedback, audit exhaustion, threshold knowledge, and correlated failure.
attack_cases.deterministic_boundary_result: Monitor output remains non-authorizing; deterministic policy still gates every sink while the evaluation measures safety and usefulness across declared adaptive strategies.

attack_cases.attack_path: tainted context or external direction -> valid API-409 handoff -> receiver proposal -> API-423 crossing -> external sink
attack_cases.why_ordinary_admission_is_insufficient: A valid controller transition can launder apparent authority or induce a trusted receiver unless labels, provenance, memory, and action admission remain independent.
attack_cases.deterministic_boundary_result: Handoff never resets labels or grants admission; controller, authority, provenance, receiver admission, crossing policy, and final sink resolve at one exact cut.

requirement_dispositions.scope: Two-coordinate participant-neutral explicit-flow authority and final-sink decision semantics.
requirement_dispositions.rationale: SEM-230 does not yet carry independent confidentiality and source-integrity coordinates transitively to every sink.

requirement_dispositions.scope: Intentional-subversion control-evaluation profiles and evidence claims.
requirement_dispositions.rationale: ASR-535 does not define attacker knowledge, adaptation, collusion, monitor topology, or audit/intervention protocols.

requirement_dispositions.scope: Participant-relative projection, exact-cut policy, memory, strategy, declassification, and noninterference boundary.
requirement_dispositions.rationale: SEM-233 refines explicit flow labels and sinks without replacing SEM-230.

requirement_dispositions.scope: Mixed-control authority, intervention, handoff, override, and cancellation semantics.
requirement_dispositions.rationale: SEM-233 keeps control changes separate from flow release and action admission.

requirement_dispositions.scope: Typed participant control occurrences and contextual validation.
requirement_dispositions.rationale: Control occurrences carry refs into the flow relation rather than becoming a second control schema.

requirement_dispositions.scope: Typed crossing request, decision, transformation, delivery, observation, and audit occurrences.
requirement_dispositions.rationale: Portable flow decisions compose at the existing crossing seam.

requirement_dispositions.scope: Authenticated supervisory lifecycle, append-only histories, replay, and atomic control transitions.
requirement_dispositions.rationale: Final-sink mediation reuses the existing identity and persistence boundary.

requirement_dispositions.scope: Reference participant crossing enforcement and durable decisions.
requirement_dispositions.rationale: Child work extends its last-boundary enforcement to SEM-233 labels and sinks.

requirement_dispositions.scope: Declared and effective participant feature support, limitations, downgrade, and conformance evidence.
requirement_dispositions.rationale: Backends need explicit flow-policy, propagation, quarantine, and sink-mediation capability posture.

requirement_dispositions.scope: Bounded participant-flow falsification, claim binding, runtime/backend evidence, and nonclaim discipline.
requirement_dispositions.rationale: ASR-536 adds intentional-subversion protocol variables without relabeling bounded ASR-535 evidence.

implementation_issues.bounded_outcome: Publish revisioned two-coordinate explicit-flow and final-sink semantic authority.
negative_cases: unknown source defaults to public or trusted
explicit_nonclaims: no model alignment, private-state, monitor-honesty, or covert-channel claim

implementation_issues.bounded_outcome: Publish closed flow-policy, label, derivation, release, sink-decision, and existing-carrier binding contracts.
evidence_required: schemas, models, fixtures, publication, and generator parity
explicit_nonclaims: contract validity is not runtime enforcement or backend realization

implementation_issues.bounded_outcome: Enforce and durably record SEM-233 immediately before every reference-runtime effect or disclosure.
negative_cases: stream, error, callback, or tool-argument bypass
deny with target call or disclosure
evidence_required: real RuntimeControlPlane and instrumented RuntimeTarget tests
both-store atomicity, idempotency, replay, and restart evidence
explicit_nonclaims: reference runtime is not backend realization
no universal IFC or covert-channel claim

implementation_issues.bounded_outcome: Declare and verify apparatus/backend flow, quarantine, monitor-topology, capability, downgrade, and realization posture.
negative_cases: gateway or monitor as sole enforcement point
different ids treated as independent monitors
evidence_required: honest, weakened, overclaiming, and correlated fixtures
explicit_nonclaims: no automatic trust in any apparatus actor
no portable LLM message, prompt, or private-state semantics

implementation_issues.bounded_outcome: Run profile-bound honest and adaptive attack evaluations with separate control mechanisms and measures.
negative_cases: ordinary negative tests promoted to intentional-subversion robustness
knowledge, adaptation, collusion, audit, or memory left implicit
unsafe hidden objective or prompt evidence
evidence_required: separate safety, usefulness, cost, uncertainty, and limitation measures
explicit_nonclaims: no model alignment or monitor-honesty claim
no result outside the exact evaluated profile

implementation_issues.bounded_outcome: Publish exact evidenced RAE runtime and harness evaluation results, limitations and nonclaims without a concrete backend prerequisite.
negative_cases: benchmark result promoted to universal robustness
apparatus details promoted to portable semantics
evidence_required: reconciled RAE runtime, fixture apparatus, and harness evaluation artifacts
explicit_nonclaims: no claim beyond the exact implemented and evaluated profiles
no automatic trust, private-reasoning, or covert-channel claim
implementation_issues.completion_gate: completed source-bound RAE harness evaluation, runtime conformance and appropriately disclosed publication; concrete backend evidence only for a separate concrete backend claim

scope_amendment.decision: RAE evaluation and publication use RAE-owned backend-neutral harnesses. Concrete backend realization is a separate conditional claim obligation; historical design observations remain unchanged.
